title: Circuit Guardian: proactive rate-escape and timeout gating
creator: Anika Rao
description: Introduce a resilient gating layer (Circuit Guardian) that proactively isolates strained regional/tiered model routes by detecting 429 bursts, request timeouts, and elevated error rates using a composite signal and soft-latch mechanism. This ticket scopes the signal definition, scoring model, API hooks for routing, and a staged rollout plan with canary + metrics-driven rollback. Goal: reduce user-facing 5xx/timeout incidents by 60% during overload while minimizing capacity churn and preserving SLOs for high-priority tenants.
background: Current routing responds reactively to spikes via route-level throttles and fallbacks. We observe noisy 429 bursts that oscillate (rapid open/close) and lead to repeated model variant evictions. Ops toil with false-positive outages because thresholds are single-signal and lack temporal smoothing. Need a multi-signal soft-latch that: 1) fuses 429, timeout, and error-rate signals; 2) decays score with tenant-aware probation; 3) exposes knobs for conservative vs aggressive tenants; 4) surfaces clear telemetry for oncall.
success_criteria: Deploy Circuit Guardian in two regions and demonstrate a >=60% reduction in user-visible timeouts during synthetic surge tests
No more than 5% increase in routed latency tail for high-priority (tier-1) customers during automated mitigation
Operational dashboard with trip-score, active isolates, and per-tenant probation state available in Console
Automated rollback if false-positive isolation rate > 1% over a 24h window
acceptance_criteria: Signal fusion implementation (429, timeout, 5xx rate) in routing layer with unit+integration tests
Soft-latch state machine with hysteresis, decay, and tenant-priority weighting implemented
Routing API accepts advisory hints from Circuit Guardian and can route to fallback model variants automatically
End-to-end load test simulating 3 classes of tenants and documented performance results
Runbook updated and oncall trained for new alerts
design_notes: Trip-score computed as weighted sum of recent 429 burstiness (short-window), timeout ratio (mid-window), and 5xx rate (long-window)
Use exponential decay for historical signals with tenant-specific half-life (tier-1: shorter half-life to recover faster; tier-3: longer probation)
Soft-latch states: CLOSED -> PROBATION -> ISOLATED -> GRACE_PERIOD -> CLOSED; transitions driven by threshold-crossings and probe successes
Expose three modes per tenant: conservative, default, aggressive; conservative delays isolation and increases revert hysteresis
Integrate with existing Variant Catalog to pick compatible fallbacks (quantized/cheaper variants) and ensure function-calling compatibility
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Library - implement signal collectors and trip-score aggregator in routing service (tests + bench)
Phase 2: State machine - implement soft-latch state store with persistence and decay logic; add tenant-priority weighting
Phase 3: API hooks - routing layer accepts advisory signals and performs non-blocking failover to pre-validated fallback variants
Phase 4: Telemetry - add trip-score metrics, isolate counts, duration histograms, and per-tenant probation state to Console
Phase 5: Load-testing and canary - run fault-injection tests, 2-region canary, monitor rollback criteria
rollout_plan: Canary: 5% of global control plane traffic in us-west-2 with conservative mode for tier-1 tenants
Observability validation: validate metrics, ensure no regression on tail latency and token costs
Expand: 25% traffic and enable default mode for tier-2, keep tier-1 conservative
Full roll: 100% with aggressive mode opt-in for internal test tenants; monitor for 72h before enabling for customers
metrics_and_telemetry: fallback_ratio: fraction of requests routed to fallback variant
false_positive_isolation_rate: post-hoc reconciled metric for rollback logic
alerts_and_thresholds: SEV1: customer_visible_timeout_rate increases by >50% vs baseline for 5m
Ops info: trip_score top-10 tenants increased by >2x in 1m
risks: Overly aggressive isolation could unnecessarily route to lower-quality variants and degrade UX
Score tuning complexity across regions and tenant mixes could require manual adjustments
Inaccurate signal attribution may isolate the wrong tenant or region (need strong correlation IDs)
Telemetry volume increase from per-request signal capture may need sampling and retention policy
